Generated from the module documentation of [`crates/canon/src/validate/mod.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/canon/blob/main/crates/canon/src/validate/mod.rs).

Deterministic validation of a `protocol/1` document.

Validation resolves every reference and reports every problem it finds, in a stable order that
does not depend on the order the sections are written in:

1. the format;
2. malformed identifiers: the protocol id, then the ids declared in artifacts, evidence kinds,
   claims, obligations, actions, outcomes, invalidation rules, case inputs and independence
   dimensions, in that section order, then the capabilities and effect classes actions name, in action order, then the
   decisions outcomes require, in outcome order, then the values case inputs declare, in input
   order;
3. duplicate identifiers, in the same section order;
4. maximum ages that are not a whole number without leading zeros, followed by `s`, `m`, `h`
   or `d`, or that are but are too long to count in seconds (each with its own message), in the
   order the evidence kinds are written;
5. case inputs that declare no value (`empty-input-values`, naming the input) or list a value
   more than once (`duplicate-input-value`, naming the input and the value, once for every
   listing after its first), in the order the inputs are written;
6. action argument schemas outside the argument-schema dialect (`action-arguments`; the dialect,
   and the order within one schema, are stated with it), each naming the action, the JSON
   Pointer of the keyword inside the schema and why it is refused, one per offending keyword,
   in the order the actions are written;
7. unresolved references and malformed input tests and order forms (a claim, an evidence kind,
   the artifact an evidence match names as its subject, which is reported after the kind it is
   written beside, then the evidence match's `independent_on`: an empty list,
   `empty-independent-on`, or a dimension it lists more than once, `duplicate-independent-on`,
   once for every listing after its first, then each dimension it lists that is not declared,
   `undeclared-dimension`, once, in the order listed, every one naming the declaration the
   match is written in; for an order form, each kind it names, `first` before `then`, then its
   subject, then a `before` whose `first` and `then` name one kind, `self-ordered-evidence`,
   naming it (an `after` may name one kind as both: a later record of a kind follows the
   first record of that kind);
   for an input test, first an empty `in` list, `empty-input-test`, or a value it lists more
   than once, `duplicate-input-test-value`, once for every listing after its first, then an
   input it names that is not declared, `undeclared-input`, or a value it lists that its input
   does not declare, `undeclared-input-value`, each value once, in the order listed, every one
   naming the declaration the test is written in and the input): those in claims first, then those
   in obligations (each obligation's discharge predicate, followed by every evidence match and
   every order form it holds, which a discharge predicate may not: it tests only claim values,
   each kind an order form names once; then its applicability predicate, followed likewise by
   every evidence match and order form it holds, `evidence-in-applicability`: it tests only
   claim values and case inputs), then those in
   actions, then those in outcomes, then those in invalidation rules (the upstream artifact,
   then each claim the rule invalidates); within a section, in the order its declarations are
   written, and within a declaration, in the order its references are written;
8. invalidation rules that name a claim reaching no evidence match, in its own predicate or in a
   claim it tests through any number of claim references (`inert-invalidation`), in the order
   the rules and their claims are written. An order form is not an evidence match here: it reads
   the history, which an invalidation rule does not change;
9. cycles between claims.

Within a section, entries come in the order they are written. Every message renders document
text on one line. The same document always yields the same problems in the same order.

## The argument-schema dialect

Generated from the module documentation of [`crates/canon/src/validate/arguments.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/canon/blob/main/crates/canon/src/validate/arguments.rs).

Canon's argument-schema dialect (story:action-arguments): the JSON Schemas an action's
`arguments` may be.

The dialect is a subset of JSON Schema 2020-12. Every schema in it is a valid 2020-12 schema
with the same meaning, so a runner can hand it to any 2020-12 validator; protocols load
offline, so it has no reference at all.

- Every schema, the top level and each nested one, names exactly one `type`: `object`,
  `array`, `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean` or `null`. The top level is `type: object`.
- `title` and `description`, strings, anywhere.
- `enum`, on any type: a non-empty list of distinct JSON scalars, each of the schema's type.
- `object`: `properties` (a map of name to schema), `required` (a list of distinct names, each
  declared in `properties`), `additionalProperties` (a boolean only).
- `array`: `items` (one schema), `minItems`, `maxItems`.
- `string`: `minLength`, `maxLength`.
- `integer` and `number`: `minimum`, `maximum`, integers.
- `minItems`, `maxItems`, `minLength` and `maxLength` are non-negative integers, and each
  minimum is at most its maximum.
- Schemas nest at most `MAX_SCHEMA_DEPTH` deep: the top level is one
  level, and each schema in `properties` or `items` one more.

Anything else is outside the dialect: `$ref`, `$defs`, `$schema`, `$id`, `allOf`, `anyOf`,
`oneOf`, `not`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `patternProperties`, `pattern`, `format`, `const`,
`exclusiveMinimum` and `exclusiveMaximum` by name, a list-valued `type`, a schema-valued
`additionalProperties`, a keyword on a type it does not apply to and any unknown keyword.

`check` reports one problem per offending keyword, at the keyword's JSON Pointer inside the
schema (an element's, for an `enum` value or a `required` name): a schema that is not an object,
names no `type` or nests too deep is reported at its own pointer. A schema whose `type` is
missing or not one of the seven has its other keywords checked only for being in the dialect,
since which apply depends on the type. Problems come in document order, the keys of every
object in code-point order, and the walk keeps a stack of its own, never recursing.

## Problem codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unsupported-format` | The document's `format` is not `protocol/1`. |
| `invalid-identifier` | An identifier is empty or contains whitespace or a control character. |
| `duplicate-identifier` | An identifier is declared more than once in one section. |
| `undeclared-claim` | A predicate tests, or an invalidation rule invalidates, a claim that is not declared. |
| `self-ordered-evidence` | A `before` order form names one evidence kind as both its `first` and its `then`: no record is observed strictly before itself. |
| `undeclared-evidence-kind` | A predicate matches or orders, or an action may produce, an evidence kind that is not declared. |
| `undeclared-artifact` | An evidence match or an order form names as its subject, or an invalidation rule as its upstream artifact, an artifact that is not declared. |
| `invalid-max-age` | An evidence kind's `max_age` is not a whole number without leading zeros, followed by `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`, or is too long to count in seconds. |
| `evidence-in-discharge` | A discharge predicate tests evidence; it may test only claim values. `path` locates the evidence match or order form inside the predicate, as `discharged_when.all[1].evidence` or `discharged_when.first`. |
| `evidence-in-applicability` | An applicability predicate tests evidence; it may test only claim values and case inputs. `path` locates the evidence match or order form inside the predicate, as `applicable_when.not.evidence` or `applicable_when.before`. |
| `empty-input-values` | A case input declares no value, so no case could give it one. |
| `duplicate-input-value` | A case input lists a value more than once. |
| `empty-input-test` | An input test lists no value, so it is false in every case. |
| `duplicate-input-test-value` | An input test lists a value more than once. |
| `undeclared-input` | An input test names an input that is not declared. |
| `undeclared-input-value` | An input test lists a value its input does not declare. |
| `empty-independent-on` | An evidence match demands independence on no dimension: `independent_on` is empty. |
| `duplicate-independent-on` | An evidence match lists a dimension in `independent_on` more than once. |
| `undeclared-dimension` | An evidence match demands independence on a dimension that is not declared. |
| `inert-invalidation` | An invalidation rule names a claim that reaches no evidence match, in its own predicate or in a claim it tests, so no record could be kept from it. |
| `claim-cycle` | Claims whose predicates test each other in a cycle; the first claim is repeated at the end. |
| `action-arguments` | An action's argument schema is outside the argument-schema dialect: `pointer` is the JSON Pointer of the offending keyword inside the schema (`""` for the schema itself) and `reason` why it is refused. |

A document that is not well-formed YAML, or not shaped like `protocol/1`, fails earlier, while parsing; the command line reports it as `parse`.
